source_document.body:

Dealer Sells a 1975 Pontiac Trans Am That Checks Almost All the Right Boxes, Numbers Matching
91 photos
Photo: Classic Auto Mall
A 1975 Pontiac Trans Am is looking for a new owner, and a dealer promises that you’ll get almost the perfect package, including matching numbers. A Trans Am that checks all the right boxes isn’t typically very hard to find, but the 1975 model year is significantly rarer.
The reason is simple. Many of these cars have already been altered - this is the case of this specimen, too, but bringing it back to a factory configuration shouldn’t be difficult - while others have ended up becoming rust buckets after years on the side of the road.
This Trans Am wears the correct paint and the screaming chicken that sets this Firebird version aside from the rest of the crowd. It’s unclear if this is the original paint, but no matter if it is, it already shows its age. It suffers from obvious bubbling, chips, and dings, so my recommendation is that you call the dealer and go see the car in person.
The dealer says there is “evidence of filler on rear fenders,” so yes, some bodywork has already been performed at some point in the past, so you’ll have to check everything thoroughly.
Photo: Classic Auto Mall The car wears an otherwise beautiful Buccaneer Red. The Trans Am color lineup was expanded to four choices in 1975, and Buccaneer Red was one of them. The rest of the choices were Sterling silver, Cameo White, and Stella Blue (whose mission was to replace Admiralty Blue).
The Trans Am was gaining ground gradually, and in 1975, it became the best-selling Firebird version in the entire line.
Pontiac sold over 84K Firebirds this year, and the Trans Am accounted for 27,274 units. The base Firebird was the runner-up with 22,293 cars, while the Esprit was third with 20,826 cars. The Formula was the last choice for Firebird buyers in 1975, getting only 13,670 orders.
The Trans Am was offered only with a 400 when the new model year was revealed, but buyers wanted more power, so Pontiac eventually reintroduced the 455 after only a few months. The 455 HO was exclusive with a 4-speed manual transmission and produced 200 horsepower.
However, the 400 continued to dominate the lineup, accounting for no more, no less than 26,417 orders. Most of these cars got an automatic transmission. Only 6,140 Trans Ams powered by an L78 were fitted with a manual.
Photo: Classic Auto Mall The same engine is also under the hood of this Trans Am, and according to the seller, this is the numbers-matching configuration. It is paired with a correct T10 4-speed manual transmission and comes alongside power brakes and power steering.
Everything is in running condition, so if you want to take the car for a short trip, you should be able to do this when you go there in person to inspect the Trans Am.
While the body shows its age, the undercarriage also requires some work. There’s surface rust and residual oil, but there’s nothing that a good metal guy wouldn’t be able to deal with. I’ve seen so many cars in worse shape getting fixed, so giving a second chance to this Trans Am shouldn’t require much effort.
The interior is the one that looks pretty cool, and the dealer says the “seat vinyl is completely intact all the way around.” Unfortunately, a previous owner decided to step away from the car’s day-one setup, so you’ll be getting an AM/FM/CD player.
Fortunately, a vintage 8-track player is also available, but please remove the CD player first because such a modern thing has no place in a classic car.
Photo: Classic Auto Mall Otherwise, this Trans Am is quite an intriguing car, especially if you’re not necessarily interested in working on it to return it to a day-one shape. This Trans Am can be driven as is, but depending on your expectations and budget, you can also spend a few more bucks to deal with all the issues I highlighted earlier.
My recommendation is that you still inspect the car live because I don’t think the photos do enough justice to this Trans Am. I wouldn’t be surprised to see the car looking even better in real person, especially because the paint doesn’t look all that bad. Buccaneer Red is a gorgeous finish anyway, especially when it’s not entirely gone.
The dealer is asking $31,900 for this Trans Am, but it also enabled the Make Offer option on eBay, so the door might be open for further negotiations. It’s up to you to make an offer the dealer can’t refuse, so click this button and reach out to the seller while you still can.
This is because the Trans Am will go offline in 4 days, unless someone clicks the Buy It Now button earlier. If you want to see this Trans Am with your own eyes, you must pack your bags and prepare for a trip to Morgantown, Pennsylvania.
